content:
[L] high | bottom ~60% of window | an enormous empty black dead zone fills the majority of the screen below the composer, reading as an unfinished/unrendered region.
[L] high | below the composer strip | the raw string "sent_text=" is exposed as literal debug output in the UI, clipped at the left window edge ("s" cut off).
[L] high | window edges | the debug text "sent_text=" is truncated at the left border, indicating content is cut off at the window edge.
[H] high | bottom black region | no content, hierarchy, or grouping exists in 60% of the frame — the screen reads as a broken render, not a product.
[C] high | whole screen | no inbox, conversation list, reading pane, or toolbar is visible at all; the "three-column" structure is entirely absent, leaving only a floating composer.
[S] med | composer strip | "Draft saved" hint on the right is much lower visual weight and small size compared to the adjacent "AI Draft" button, creating an unbalanced header row.
[C] med | composer footer | the label "tools" floats alone with no grouping, controls, or visual connection to anything — reads as a placeholder/debug label.
[H] med | composer body | "To: kim@example.com" is plain unstyled text at the same visual weight as body copy, with no label styling or field affordance.
[S] med | composer body | the reply textarea is very tall (~110px) for a two-word draft "draft text", wasting vertical space while the rest of the screen is empty.
[H] low | footer row | "reply — sent to the customer · Ctrl+Enter sends" mixes state text and shortcut hint at equal low weight in one run-on line.
[S] low | top-right controls | "Saved Replies" and "AI Draft" buttons sit close together with tight gaps inconsistent with the large whitespace elsewhere.
[S] low | composer left inset | footer text starts at a slightly different left inset than the "To:" line above it.

VERDICT: unprofessional — a lone composer floats above a giant black void with leaked debug text ("sent_text=") clipped at the window edge; this is a broken render, not a shippable screen.
